DASCore provides several tools to help coding agents use it more effectively. Start by installing the skills and have your agent explore the API.

## Install the skills

### With library-skills

DASCore ships its skills in `dascore/.agents/skills/`, the layout [library-skills](https://pypi.org/project/library-skills/) reads. From a project whose environment has DASCore installed, run:

```bash
uvx library-skills
```

It finds the skills of the project's dependencies and asks which to link into `.agents/skills`. Claude Code reads only `.claude/skills`, so add `--claude` for it.

Or just ask your agent:

> Run `uvx library-skills --claude --all -y` to install the DASCore skills into this project.

## Included skills

`dascore` is the entry point: it finds the APIs and workflows of the DASCore installed in your project.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from dascore.utils.doc_skills import get_skills

DEVELOPMENT = "DASCore development. "
SKILL_FILES = "https://github.com/DASDAE/dascore/blob/dev/dascore/.agents/skills"


def skill_table(development):
    """Print the user or development skills as a table, from the skill files."""
    print("| Skill | Documentation | Purpose |\n| --- | --- | --- |")
    for name, info in get_skills().items():
        purpose = info["description"]
        if purpose.startswith(DEVELOPMENT) != development:
            continue
        target = info["target"]
        href = f"../{target}.qmd" if target else f"{SKILL_FILES}/{name}/SKILL.md"
        purpose = purpose.removeprefix(DEVELOPMENT)
        print(f"| `{name}` | [{info['title']}]({href}) | {purpose} |")


skill_table(development=False)
```

Run `dascore skills` to list available workflows, or `dascore skill <name>` to read one. Each link is the same procedure served by the CLI. The annotation and beta-testing skills are written for agents and have no docs page, so their links go to the skill files; the [annotations tutorial](annotations.qmd) covers the same tools for people. The migration and beta-testing skill files can also be given directly to an agent without installing the skill.

## Development skills

These are for work on DASCore itself; their descriptions begin with "DASCore development".

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
skill_table(development=True)
```

## Where skills live

Every skill is a `SKILL.md` file under `dascore/.agents/skills/` in the installed package, where tools that link skills from a project's dependencies find them.
